claim: S3 delivers strong read-after-write consistency automatically, at no additional cost and without changes to performance or availability.
question: What consistency model does Amazon S3 provide?

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 delivers strong read-after-write consistency automatically, without changes to performance or availability, without sacrificing regional isolation for applications, and at no additional cost.

claim: After a successful write of a new object or an overwrite of an existing object, any subsequent read immediately receives the latest version of the object.
question: What does a read return right after a successful PUT or overwrite in S3?

evidence.quote: After a successful write of a new object or an overwrite of an existing object, any subsequent read request immediately receives the latest version of the object.

claim: S3 also gives strong consistency for list operations: after a write, a listing of the bucket immediately reflects the change.
question: Are S3 list operations strongly consistent?

evidence.quote: S3 also provides strong consistency for list operations, so after a write, you can immediately perform a listing of the objects in a bucket with any changes reflected.

claim: S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for PUT and DELETE requests of objects in all AWS Regions, for new objects, overwrites and deletes.
question: Does S3 strong consistency cover DELETE requests and overwrites, and in which Regions?

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for PUT and DELETE requests of objects in your Amazon S3 bucket in all AWS Regions. This behavior applies to both writes of new objects as well as PUT requests that overwrite existing objects and DELETE requests.

claim: S3 is designed to handle traffic for any internet application; its scale spreads the load so that no individual application is affected by traffic spikes.
question: What happens to S3 performance when application traffic suddenly spikes?

values.display: no individual application is affected by traffic spikes

evidence.quote: Amazon S3’s massive scale lets you spread the load evenly, so that no individual application is affected by traffic spikes.

claim: The S3 SLA provides a service credit if the monthly uptime percentage falls below the service commitment in any billing cycle.
question: What does the Amazon S3 SLA give you when availability falls short?

evidence.quote: The Amazon S3 SLA provides for a service credit if a customer's monthly uptime percentage is below our service commitment in any billing cycle.

claim: S3 Standard is designed for 99.99% availability; S3 Standard-IA, S3 Intelligent-Tiering and S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for 99.9%; S3 One Zone-IA for 99.5%; S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive for 99.99% availability with an SLA of 99.9%.
question: What availability is each S3 storage class designed for?

values.spoken: ninety-nine point nine nine percent availability

evidence.quote: The S3 Standard storage class is designed for 99.99% availability, the S3 Standard-IA storage class, S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class, and the S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval storage classes are designed for 99.9% availability, the S3 One Zone-IA storage class is designed for 99.5% availability, and the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive class are designed for 99.99% availability and an SLA of 99.9%.

claim: S3 One Zone-IA offers a 99% available SLA and is designed for eleven 9’s of durability within its Availability Zone.
question: What availability SLA does S3 One Zone-IA carry?

qualifiers.scope: S3 One Zone-IA, per billing cycle

evidence.quote: S3 One Zone-IA offers a 99% available SLA and is also designed for eleven 9’s of durability within the Availability Zone.

claim: An individual S3 object can range in size from a minimum of 0 bytes to a maximum of 50 TB.
question: What is the minimum and maximum size of one S3 object?

evidence.quote: Individual Amazon S3 objects can range in size from a minimum of 0 bytes to a maximum of 50 TB.

note: FAQ value; older material says 5 TB. The changes lens re-grounds the date of the increase.

claim: The largest object that can be uploaded in a single PUT is 5 GB.
question: How large can an object be in a single PUT request?

evidence.quote: The largest object that can be uploaded in a single PUT is 5 GB.

claim: For objects larger than 100 MB, AWS says customers should consider multipart upload.
question: From what object size does AWS recommend multipart upload?

evidence.quote: For objects larger than 100 MB, customers should consider using the multipart upload capability.

claim: The total volume of data and the number of objects you can store in S3 are unlimited.
question: Is there a limit on how much data or how many objects an S3 bucket can hold?

evidence.quote: The total volume of data and number of objects you can store in Amazon S3 are unlimited.

claim: A single general purpose bucket can hold objects in all storage classes except S3 Express One Zone; general purpose buckets are recommended for most use cases.
question: Which storage classes can a general purpose bucket hold?

values.display: all storage classes except S3 Express One Zone

evidence.quote: General purpose buckets are the original S3 bucket type, and a single general purpose bucket can contain objects stored across all storage classes except S3 Express One Zone. They are recommended for most use cases and access patterns.

claim: Directory buckets only allow objects in the S3 Express One Zone storage class, which processes data within a single Availability Zone.
question: Which storage class can a directory bucket hold?

values.display: only allow objects stored in the S3 Express One Zone storage class

evidence.quote: S3 directory buckets only allow objects stored in the S3 Express One Zone storage class, which provides faster data processing within a single Availability Zone. They are recommended for low-latency use cases.

claim: Each directory bucket can support up to 2 million transactions per second (TPS), independent of the number of directories in the bucket.
question: How many transactions per second can one S3 directory bucket support?

evidence.quote: Each S3 directory bucket can support up to 2 million transactions per second (TPS), independent of the number of directories within the bucket.

claim: A table bucket is purpose-built for storing tables in the Apache Iceberg format.
question: What is an S3 table bucket for?

evidence.quote: A table bucket is purpose-built for storing tables using the Apache Iceberg format.

claim: A vector bucket is purpose-built for storing and querying vectors through dedicated vector APIs, not the S3 object APIs.
question: What is an S3 vector bucket for?

evidence.quote: Within a vector bucket, you do not use the S3 object APIs, but rather dedicated vector APIs to write vector data and query it based on semantic meaning and similarity.

note: S3 Vectors GA date must be checked by the changes lens; may be not examinable yet.

claim: Normal S3 rates apply for every version of an object stored or requested.
question: How is S3 Versioning billed?

evidence.quote: Normal Amazon S3 rates apply for every version of an object stored or requested.

claim: Normal S3 pricing applies when another AWS account accesses your storage, unless you configure the bucket as Requester Pays, in which case the requester pays for requests and downloads.
question: Who pays when another AWS account accesses your S3 bucket?

evidence.quote: Normal Amazon S3 pricing applies when your storage is accessed by another AWS Account. Alternatively, you may choose to configure your bucket as a Requester Pays bucket, in which case the requester will pay the cost of requests and downloads of your Amazon S3 data.

claim: There is no data transfer charge between Amazon EC2 (or any AWS service) and S3 within the same Region.
question: Is data transfer between EC2 and S3 in the same Region charged?

evidence.quote: There is no Data Transfer charge for data transferred between Amazon EC2 (or any AWS service) and Amazon S3 within the same Region, for example, data transferred within the US East (Northern Virginia) Region.

claim: Data transfer costs are billed to the source bucket owner.
question: Who is billed for S3 data transfer costs?

evidence.quote: Data transfer costs are billed to the source bucket owner.

claim: There is no data transfer charge for a COPY within one S3 Region; a COPY between Regions is charged at the pricing page rates.
question: Is an S3 COPY request charged for data transfer?

evidence.quote: There is no Data Transfer charge for data transferred within an Amazon S3 Region via a COPY request. Data transferred via a COPY request between AWS Regions is charged at rates specified on the Amazon S3 pricing page.

claim: With S3 you pay only for what you use; there is no minimum charge.
question: Does S3 have a minimum charge?

evidence.quote: With Amazon S3, you pay only for what you use. There is no minimum charge.

claim: AWS offers eligible customers free data transfer out to the internet when they move all of their data off AWS.
question: Is data transfer out charged when you move all your data off AWS?

values.display: free data transfer out to the internet

evidence.quote: AWS offers eligible customers free data transfer out to the internet when they move all of their data off of AWS, in accordance with the process below.
